summary: Adams County tower planned in 1931 and listed complete by May 1932; a 2004 tornado damaged or destroyed it and it was rebuilt in 2009; listed standing, undated.

events.note: Listed as already completed in a May 1932 newspaper item quoted by the Forest Lookouts page; a December 1931 notice said four district towers were nearly finished. Builder and design not in the sources read.
June 23, 2004 tornado damaged trees and the lookout tower (Forest Lookouts log). The 2015 Star News article says the tower was destroyed. The sources disagree on the extent of the loss.
New tower erected; the Star News gives a cost of over $300,000. The log places the completed rebuild in June 2009.
DNR announced in December 2015 a plan to close all of its remaining fire towers. Statewide decision as reported by the Star News; no Quincy-specific outcome given.

notes_for_editor: Built year 1932 rests on a May 1932 newspaper item quoted by a Forest Lookouts page; the original newspaper was not read. The 2004 damage conflict is unresolved: the log says damaged, the 2015 Star News says destroyed. No height, design, staffing or access source found. Standing status is from an undated FFLA list and was not confirmed after the 2015 closure plan. Record agency 'Conservation Department' is the historic name; the 1931 notice names the Wisconsin conservation commission. The 'destroyed' claim is the Star News reporter's wording, citing Schumacher as an example; the cost and 2009 date come from the same article. The SNA page and blog describe the natural area, not the tower's exact position.
